learningCurve.reason: durable observation, procedural, route-choice, trace, and model-runtime observation records append to Store logs; project_learning_from_store now replays those logs into a deterministic Store-derived learning and recurrence projection

dogfoodLessons.lesson: The local runtime contract is backend-neutral, but the first-class path is llama-cpp/GGUF, not ONNX-first.
Contract proof and execution proof are different things; a degraded/default build is honest, but it is not parity.
Token reduction can be real even when reranker lift is still zero, so those metrics must be tracked separately.
Model observations stay append-only first, then project into graph/memory views; the proof must distinguish persisted observation facts from derived graph curves.
A broad QA runner can create fabricated red by claiming rows it cannot prove; runner claim logic must be fixture-backed and leave unsupported rows unrunnable.
Runtime model proof must be CPU-first and one-model-at-a-time by default; GPU/NPU requires provider probes and child-process timeout protection.
Rollup proof must be derived from artifact evidence; stale pending rows can hide completed model, token, Store, RAG, dogfood, and parity work just as badly as fabricated green can overclaim it.
When a prefix flips from pending to artifact-backed green, rollup tests must update the derived signal assertion instead of preserving stale false expectations.
Coordination lane ids are not Git branch names; slash-bearing branch names must be recorded as branch metadata while lane uses a schema-valid id.
Compile-green harness changes can still violate test policy; no-test-doubles and weak-assertions must run on touched test files before commit.

Store-backed learning projection should clone a seed lesson graph and replay canonical Store observation logs into that projection; otherwise recurrence proof either mutates caller state or treats the in-memory graph as the source of truth.

Repo-local GGUF proof harnesses must discover direct llama.cpp worker binaries, not only llama-cli, because embedding proof must use an Enforcer-owned route such as llama-embedding and reject llama-server as an external API surface.

Exact MCP parity rows should stay on the exact-evidence allowlist when the repo can prove a tool's registry, router, and smoke-test surface mechanically; otherwise the broad MCP runner understates landed parity as unrunnable.
Exact CLI parity rows should only flip green when the row-specific command path, handler wiring, and deterministic test/doc evidence all line up; nearby generic CLI proof is not enough.

Native `enforcer` CLI rows must stay distinct from legacy `.mjs` surfaces; when the row names the Rust CLI, prove it with the Rust binary-name seam and Rust fixture tests rather than nearby compatibility shims.
Artifact-backed parity rows are acceptable when the artifact itself already encodes the exact cross-surface claim and the named evidence tests prove that claim mechanically.

A CLI `run --tool ...` parity row should only flip green when command dispatch, tool-language routing, parser proof, integration test coverage, and operator-facing docs all line up on the same tool path.
Real full-matrix QA proof is heavyweight; repeated architecture/repository indexing must reuse cached per-target evidence or the harness turns proof regeneration into avoidable repeated work.

Claude adapter selection is narrower than Claude install-hook parity; keep the hook proof row blocked, but allow the adapter-selection row to go green when harness key, selection core, detection, and fixture coverage all line up.

Some semantic-looking QA rows can still be proven by exact structural evidence when the row maps to a single concrete mechanism such as route traces, lifecycle telemetry, or deferred-work validation fixtures.
Benchmark rows that explicitly name root workspace config facts should use that config as the single source of truth instead of widening into synthesized repository summaries.

Exact QA rows scored at Recall@5 cannot dump every exhaustive match as the row id set; exhaustive repository scans need one summary id plus full sourceRefs, or honest evidence will fail the harness for the wrong reason.

Exact structural parity probes must follow the code's real seam names; inventing a plausible constructor like `RepoRoot::new(cwd)` fabricates red even when the repo already proves the current `parse::<RepoRoot>()` path.

Low-cost QA promotions should bind to concrete append/read seams that already exist, such as coordination ledger append helpers and NDJSON reader/writer APIs, instead of widening a whole category runner just to flip a few rows.

A green subpack artifact plus named proof tests is sufficient for exact parity promotion when the row asks for that exact subpack behavior; federation rows do not need a synthetic generic runner when the artifact and roundtrip tests already encode the claim.

Doc-backed parity probes must distinguish plan intent from current repo truth: when a benchmark names an ownership chain and the implementation still lives in a transitional file, prove both the live definition and the owning workpack instead of pretending the planned file split already landed.

A GGUF embedding proof is not honest unless it records which llama.cpp route actually ran and validates the returned embedding dimension contract; fallback-by-side-effect and any nonempty vector are both fake green.

Cheap GitHistory QA promotions should bind to specific git facts the repo can prove now, such as unchanged single-commit fixture files or the latest add-bearing commit on the active lane, instead of waiting for a broad history summarizer.

When benchmark prose and the current QA proof gate diverge, exact-evidence promotions must follow the live proof gate rows and then prove those rows with concrete artifact or snippet evidence instead of relying on older category prose.

Default degraded runtime status must remain source-policy-aware: unconfigured sources should report unavailable/model-source-unconfigured, local-cache defaults should report unavailable/artifact-not-installed, and bundled or parent-installed assets should degrade as integrity-unverified instead of collapsing everything to a generic artifact-missing state.

Exact QA promotions can mine plan/docs/git truth when the row names a specific prior incident or proven pattern; that is better than leaving the row unrunnable or widening a broad category runner past its evidence.

Continuous-learning and federation proof surfaces can promote broad-looking QA rows honestly when the row maps to a small deterministic fixture or artifact seam; that is cheaper and safer than expanding a generic category runner too early.

When exact QA promotions depend on live proof or source text, the harness should be allowed to reject stale markers first; tightening the probe to the current file contents is safer than keeping a broader but drift-prone interpretation.

Rows that prove large result sets or self-referential rollups need bounded summary ids and qualitative invariants; otherwise ranking metrics or artifact-regeneration timing can create false red or stale proof.

Checked-in runtime artifacts are not canonical proof until they carry proofScope, appear in the aggregate proof graph, and have row-specific semantic assertions; broad no-hardcoded-path and ciParity scans are necessary but not sufficient.

Exact CodeGraph promotions should use bounded summary ids backed by manifests or hot-path source markers; if a probe dumps too many concrete ids into a top-k scored row, the harness will correctly fail ranking even when the evidence itself is true.

Exact Symbol promotions are honest when a row maps to one stable function with a bounded callee set; prefer small call-edge summary ids over broad workspace symbol sweeps when the benchmark question is local and deterministic.

Broad-looking error-surface rows can still be promoted honestly when the crate collapses them into a few stable boundary families; summary ids over validated boundary groups are safer than pretending the harness can enumerate every raw symbol return site.

Lesson-retrieval rows must return lesson ids, not observation ids; use observations only to prove the lesson linkage. If the probe returns the wrong semantic entity, the harness should and will mark the row false-red.

Dependency-policy exceptions must be executable policy, not prose-only policy. If deny.toml records a narrow RUSTSEC exception, the Enforcer runner must pass that exact exception to cargo audit and keep unmaintained=deny for everything else.

Exact-evidence QA rows must follow migrated proof files after required-tests cleanup. Production source markers and migrated unit-test markers are both valid evidence, but the row must point at the file that actually owns each marker.

ORT ownership needs an executable worker command seam, not only a serializable plan. The Enforcer-owned command must carry task/provider as args, model and tokenizer metadata as env, and avoid server or port surfaces by construction.

Runtime proof JSON should be derived from typed runtime ownership contracts. If the probe hand-writes ownership data, it can drift from the code that actually validates llama.cpp and ORT lifecycle control.

Real-model probe compile gates are required even when default CI stays zero-network. They catch runtime-only assumptions such as stale helper imports that ordinary default-model tests do not exercise.

followUps: Checked-in real model runtime proofs remain host-local and non-CI-parity; rerun explicit probes when hardware, cache, or providers change.

QA coverage is 250/250 green with 0 failures in proof/memory/x06-rag-qa.json and proof/memory/x06-feature-parity.json; keep unsupported future install-hook rows outside X06 memory scope unless new code lands.

Full cargo test -p enforcer-memory --quiet -j 1 exceeded a 60 minute local timeout after QA-013 was fixed; keep using focused suites as evidence until the broad package suite is split, sharded, or its long-running target set is isolated.
recurrenceNotes: t0 events now have durable Store append paths for observations and model-runtime incidents.
t1 proof exists through Store replay tests and clean source-shape/check gates.
t2 recurrence curves now come from project_learning_from_store, which replays Store logs into a deterministic projection before computing learning_curve and recurrence_curve.
